title: App events into the warehouse by morning
summary: Collect app events reliably and have correct numbers ready before the 9:00 meeting.
context: Hoodi Hops, a food and drinks app, sends about 3 billion events a day from phones and web. Analysts run daily reports from a warehouse, and leadership reads them at 9:00. Phones may send events hours late, and some send them twice.
Each app team adds events freely. Last month someone renamed a field and revenue on the dashboard fell by half for two days before anyone noticed.
must_handle: Late events still land in the right day, and the report says what it has counted.
A changed or broken event is caught before the report goes out.
A failed job can rerun for one day without touching others.
Raw events are kept cheaply for 90 days for replays.
show_in_answer: The journey of one event from a phone to a report.
How storage is laid out, and what it costs.
How late and duplicate events are treated.
Where a broken schema is caught, and who hears about it.
